answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit work, with rewards and reputation tied to that same locked stake. If a cluster of fake agents tries to wander through the system, their shared deposits remain visible and can be slashed when a challenge proves coordinated fraud. This raises the cost of each Sybil identity: the attacker must buy and immobilize more capital, while honest agents can harbor trust across tasks rather than restart from scratch. A copied identity adds no stake, so its echo cannot claim an independent history.
